title: Anand Deverakonda and Vaishnavi Chaitanya Reunite for 'EPIC: First Semester' on September 11
excerpt: The 'Baby' duo's campus romance, backed by Sithara Entertainments, locks a September release date with strong pre-release buzz and a clear theatrical runway.
body:
• EPIC: First Semester, starring Anand Deverakonda and Vaishnavi Chaitanya, has locked September 11, 2026 as its worldwide theatrical release date.
  • The film reunites the lead pair from the 2023 sleeper hit Baby, which crossed Rs 20 crore at the box office and became a Gen Z favourite.
  • Directed by debutant Aditya Haasan (known for the acclaimed web series 90s), it is a coming-of-age campus romance about NRI students studying abroad.
  • The release slot opened up after Vijay Deverakonda's Ranabaali was reportedly delayed from the same window.

Anand Deverakonda and Vaishnavi Chaitanya are reuniting for EPIC: First Semester, a Telugu romantic drama set for a worldwide theatrical release on September 11, 2026. The film is produced by Suryadevara Naga Vamsi and Sai Soujanya under the Sithara Entertainments and Fortune Four Cinemas banners.

The announcement has generated significant buzz in the Telugu film industry, primarily because of the lead pair's track record. Their 2023 collaboration Baby started as a modest campus romance but snowballed into a surprise hit, crossing the Rs 20 crore share mark at the box office and resonating deeply with younger audiences.

A Coming-of-Age NRI Story

Directed by Aditya Haasan, whose acclaimed web series 90s established him as a sharp storyteller of youth narratives, EPIC: First Semester is a coming-of-age drama centred on NRI students navigating love, friendships, peer pressure, and self-discovery at an overseas college.

At promotional events, Anand Deverakonda revealed that the story struck a personal chord, drawing from his own experiences of studying abroad. He described it as an emotionally relatable drama that goes beyond typical campus romance tropes to explore themes of family expectations, cultural identity, and growing up far from home.

Veteran actors Shivaji and Vasuki Anand round out the cast in key supporting roles, adding emotional depth to the youth-centric narrative.

Music and Technical Team

Hesham Abdul Wahab, the composer behind several recent Malayalam and Telugu chartbusters, has scored the film's album. Early song releases have already drawn positive attention, with industry observers noting the soulful, understated quality that characterised the Baby soundtrack.

Cinematographer Azeem Mohammad handles the visuals, while editor Navin Nooli — a seasoned hand in Telugu cinema — manages the post-production. The technical team's pedigree has strengthened expectations for a polished theatrical experience.

A Fortuitous Release Window

The September 11 date carries strategic significance. Industry reports indicate that the slot became available after Vijay Deverakonda's Ranabaali, which was initially planned for the same window, was pushed back as production continued. With minimal major Telugu releases competing in early September, EPIC: First Semester has a clear theatrical runway.

Trade analysts have highlighted the favourable timing: the film targets college students and family audiences during the September festive window, and Sithara Entertainments' distribution network — one of the strongest in the Telugu market — ensures wide screen availability.

Why Baby Worked

Baby succeeded because of its restraint. Instead of manufactured drama, the 2023 film offered a grounded, realistic portrayal of young love that connected with Gen Z viewers through word of mouth rather than star power or spectacle. The Anand-Vaishnavi pairing became an overnight sensation, with their understated chemistry cited as the film's defining quality.

EPIC: First Semester is built on the same foundation — relatable characters, a campus setting, emotional authenticity — but with a larger canvas. The NRI angle opens the story to diaspora audiences who see their own experiences reflected in characters negotiating two cultures simultaneously.

What's Ahead

The makers are planning a promotional push with campus tours, a late-August trailer launch, and college-themed events in the weeks before release. While the official release date has been widely reported at September 11, the makers have not yet issued a formal confirmation — though all industry indicators point to the date holding.

For Anand Deverakonda, the film represents a critical big-screen comeback after a relatively quiet stretch following Baby. A strong opening could establish the actor as a consistent draw in Telugu cinema's competitive mid-budget space.
